previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis and recent coronary stenting was admitted for lower abdominal pain, vomiting, and diarrhea. Initial evaluation revealed elevated cardiac enzymes and EKG changes concerning for NSTEMI, prompting a cardiac catheterization that showed in-stent restenosis of the right coronary artery, which was treated with a new drug-eluting stent. Abdominal CT suggested infectious enterocolitis, and the patient was treated with ciprofloxacin and metronidazole, with resolution of symptoms. Markedly elevated CK levels indicated rhabdomyolysis, likely due to simvastatin, which was discontinued along with colchicine. The patient improved clinically, with decreasing CK and resolution of abdominal symptoms, and was discharged home on dual antiplatelet therapy and antibiotics, with plans for outpatient follow-up and CK monitoring.

INDICATION:  ___ man with coronary artery disease, gout, anterior
tibialis tendon tenosynovitis, presenting with inability to ambulate due to
anterior ankle pain.  Presenting for ultrasound-guided aspiration and
therapeutic steroid injection.

COMPARISON:  Not available at the ___.  Note is made of MR dated ___.

FINDINGS/TECHNIQUE:

Preliminary targeted grayscale and color Doppler scanning of the anterior
tibialis tendon demonstrates marked thickening of the tendon, which measures
up to 1.6 cm in diameter.  The thickening is focal, at the level of the
tibiotalar joint. It is very heterogeneous in echogenicity. At the posterior
aspect of the tibialis anterior tendon, there is focal surfacing
hypoechogenicity.  Findings are compatible with severe tendinosis with small
partial thickness tear posteriorly.

There is hypoechoic material surrounding the tendon, in addition to some
rounded intermediate echogenicity material in the tibialis anterior tendon
sheath compatible with tenosynovitis and debris.

After discussion with Dr. ___ decision was made to proceed with
ultrasound-guided aspiration of the synovial tendon sheath fluid for crystal
analysis, but not to perform injection in view of partial thickness tear.

After discussion of risks, the benefits, and alternatives of the proposed
procedure, written informed consent was obtained from the patient.  A
preprocedure timeout was performed, using three patient identifiers.

Skin was marked with ultrasound guidance.  It was then prepped and draped in
usual sterile fashion.  1% lidocaine was administered to anesthetize the skin
and subcutaneous tissues.  Subsequently, a 25-gauge needle and also 22-gauge
needle (two passes) were advanced into the tendon sheath of the anterior
tibialis tendon under continuous sonographic guidance, and 0.5 mL of
serosanguineous fluid was aspirated.

Needle was then removed, hemostasis achieved, and a dry sterile dressing
applied.

The patient tolerated the procedure well, there were no immediate
complications.

Dr. ___, the attending radiologist, was present and supervised the
entire procedure.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Status post ultrasound-guided aspiration of the tendon sheath of the
anterior tibialis tendon. fluid sent for crystal analysis.
2.  Marked tendinopathy and small partial tear posteriorly of the anterior
tibialis tendon at the level of the tibiotalar joint.
